Q: How to force clang assembler to emit the `rex.W` prefix? A:

With GNU as, you can just write the prefix normally:

rex.W psllq $12, %xmm1

This is exactly how GNU binutils will disassemble the opcode bytes you have given. To check this, you can create a file psllq.s with the contents

.byte 0x66, 0x48, 0x0f, 0x73, 0xf1, 0x0c

then run as psllq.s -o psllq.o && objdump -d psllq.o to obtain:


psllq.o:     file format elf64-x86-64


Disassembly of section .text:

0000000000000000 <.text>:
   0:   66 48 0f 73 f1 0c       rex.W psllq $0xc,%xmm1

If you then replace the contents of the assembly file with the disassembled instruction rex.W psllq $0xc,%xmm1 and assemble it back, the object code will be identical.

LLVM, however, does not seem to accept an explicitly written down prefix, and llvm-objdump will not even show one in the disassembly. You will be resigned to writing out the whole instruction as a .byte directive.

Q: Selenium opens page in the Chrome footer A:

Using WPF and C# with Selenium you must be using the recently released google-chrome Version 145.0.7632.76 (Official Build). In that case for optimal performance you should be using the latest Selenium version Stable: 4.40.0 (January 18, 2026).

Using Selenium v4.40.0 you can leverage the automated driver and browser management for Selenium through Selenium Manager the command-line tool implemented in Rust.

Advantages

Using Selenium Manager you neither have to explicitly initiate CreateDefaultService() nor have to pass the service argument while initializing the Chrome browser. Additionally the matching version of Selenium & Chrome browser is thoroughly tested to provide optimum results.

Headless --screen-info switch for Headless Chrome

In the discussion Setting window resolution via chrome_options.add_argument("--window-size=1920,1080") does not work it is clearly mentioned:

Starting with m135 Chrome Headless Mode on Linux (m136 on Windows and m138 on Macs) stopped using physical screen parameters as the basis for UI geometry calculations. Instead, it uses a virtual 800x600 headless screen that is completely independent of any physical screen attached to the system the Headless Chrome is running on. The --window-size switch now only defines the initial browser window size, and not the headless screen size as it was before with Chrome Headless Shell.

So replacing:

driver.Manage().Window.Maximize();
driver.Manage().Window.FullScreen();

with:

--screen-info={1920x1080}

should fix your problem.

Effectively your lines of code will be:

if ((bool)RunParams.IsHeadless)
{
    chromeOptions.AddArgument("--headless=new");
    chromeOptions.AddArgument("--screen-info={1920x1080}");
}

References

You can find a relevant detailed discussion in:

  • Selenium with chromedriver blank (White) screenshots in headless mode (Working on firefox)

Q: Avrdude flash fails on MacOS Monterey A:

My research on the errors from avrdude suggested it was a FTDI driver issue on older MacOS. I fixed the problem. You had to hold down RBUTTON on the Chameleon Mini RevG while powering on to put it in bootloader mode. Then the firmware can be flashed. PEBKAC-type error, I guess: Problem exists between keyboard and chair.
